scenes.rationale: Repeated diffuse spheres spread across the visible field under one small area emitter. Similar surface/light structure is intended to limit spatial allocation advantage; uniform noise is not assumed or measured.

A staggered field of equal diffuse spheres and two equally bright compact emitters is an independent layout intended to distribute difficult illumination broadly. No noise statistic has been inspected.

A smooth dielectric sphere between smooth conducting spheres, illuminated by a compact emitter, is intended to expose rare specular/transmission paths and uncertain estimates without asserting measured variance.

An independent offset arrangement of three dielectric spheres and a large conductor behind them creates multiple reflection/transmission opportunities. Compact lighting makes long/rare contributions plausible, not proven.
Three diffuse spheres with a point source and uniform background use cheap conventional surface transport; the scene intentionally provides no asserted controller benefit.
Two original diffuse tetrahedral meshes and a diffuse sphere form a separate inexpensive geometry/light layout with no specular material in use.
A foreground diffuse occluder crosses the view and changes visibility of fixed surfaces and a rear emitter at three exact times. Each frame is an independent static render, with no temporal reuse.

Two independently moving specular/transmissive objects and a depth-changing diffuse object alter occlusion and path structure in a separate three-frame layout. Frame differences are geometric definitions, not measured temporal advantages.

A broad diffuse surface region contrasts with a compact glass/conductor cluster and small emitter on one side. Spatially uneven transport is intended to give competent conventional adaptivity an opportunity, without claiming measured superiority.

An isolated rough-dielectric and conductor patch is set against several diffuse objects under broad background illumination and one bright localized source. This independent arrangement intends heterogeneous difficulty, not a policy-tuned challenge.
